title: A counter loses increments
hook: A Java service counts accepted requests. With eight worker threads, the displayed count is lower than the number of accepted requests.
context: Single JVM request handler with a shared metric counter
solution_brief: counter++ is read-modify-write, so concurrent increments are lost. AtomicLong.incrementAndGet provides atomic updates and visibility for this single-JVM metric. LongAdder often scales better for high contention with a non-atomic aggregate read; neither coordinates across hosts.

steps.prompt: What race exists in the code?

options.text: Two threads can read the same value and overwrite one another’s increment
The JVM always serializes ++ on shared fields
The counter overflows after eight requests

steps.explanation: A is the lost-update race. B is false: ++ is read, add, write. C is unrelated to this small workload.
steps.bottleneck_note: volatile alone gives visibility, not atomic read-modify-write.
steps.code_snippet:
static long count;
void accepted() { count++; }

steps.prompt: If both threads read 7 before either writes, what value can the field hold after both increments?
steps.explanation: A occurs when both write 8. B needs serialized increments. C would require adding the old values rather than one each.
steps.bottleneck_note: The lost update is observable despite both handlers completing.
steps.context_note: Both workers have already read the old value.

steps.prompt: Which replacement gives atomic increments and a consistent value on this JVM?
steps.explanation: A performs an atomic update. B exposes writes but still loses simultaneous increments. C changes no behavior.
steps.bottleneck_note: Choose the primitive based on the required consistency of reads.
steps.context_note: The product needs an exact count at read time.

steps.prompt: Contention grows to hundreds of threads, and the dashboard tolerates a non-atomic aggregate snapshot. What may improve throughput?

options.text: Use a new AtomicLong in each request

steps.explanation: A spreads increments across cells; sum is not an atomic snapshot. B broadens contention. C loses the shared total.
steps.bottleneck_note: LongAdder trades exact point-in-time reads for scalable updates.
steps.context_note: The exact-read requirement has been relaxed.

steps.prompt: The service now runs on three hosts. What does AtomicLong count?

options.text: Only increments in its own JVM; combine durable events or a shared counter for a global total
All hosts automatically because the class is static
Only requests from the first thread

steps.explanation: A recognizes process boundaries. B confuses static per JVM with global state. C is unrelated to AtomicLong.
steps.bottleneck_note: Thread safety does not provide distributed coordination.
steps.context_note: Traffic is load-balanced across three processes.
